Radomsko Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Radomsko, Poland

Not demolished. Jewish settlement in Radomsko developed after Poland's Third Partition; an independent synagogue supervision formed in 1834, and the town became seat of its own Hasidic dynasty from the 19th century. By 1921, 7,774 (41%) were mostly murdered at Treblinka in 1942-1943. This cemetery, established between 1805-1832 per varying sources, holds the ohel of tzadik Szlomo ha-Kohen Rabinowicz (buried 1866), founder of the local Hasidic dynasty, with subsequent Rabinowicz family members buried nearby. During WWII, the site witnessed mass executions - several dozen killed in October 1942, about 1,500 more in early January 1943. Postwar oversight passed from the Częstochowa Mosaic Faith Congregation to today's Jewish Community in Łódź; the cemetery remains one of Poland's few still active, with its last burial in 1990. A 2017 Hasidic center with prayer room, mikveh, and hotel opened alongside the grounds to serve visiting pilgrims.
